judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'Related Party Loans' turns on affiliation 'with the Manager, the Members, or the Servicer ... or their family members', an open-ended class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c064's last sentence and c058's last sentence both carve transactions out of the Related Party Loan definition, so the definition here is not self-contained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall not exceed 20% of total Company assets at such time' is a definite, continuously-tested covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c073 restates the identical limit as tested only 'upon the closing of the Related Party Loan in question' — a continuous test against a point-in-time test is a direct inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'consistent with the lending standards and policies set forth above and with loan terms typically offered by the Company on similar loans to unaffiliated borrowers' is doubly vague — which standards, and what is 'typically offered' by a company with no operating history.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'set forth above' points backwards from Section III to the Section IV lending criteria that actually follow it, so the cross-reference does not fit the document's order.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any material event of default' is undefined, and 'has occurred and is continuing for ninety (90) consecutive days' can be read as running from occurrence or from materiality.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c073 states the same buy-back obligation as arising 'if the Loan is in default more than 90 days', dropping the materiality qualifier — the two formulations do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive conflicts disclosure; 'after consideration of all relevant factors, including...' is an open list but plainly illustrative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'Other Sponsored Investment Funds' but the document then uses 'Other Sponsored Funds' and 'Sponsored Investment Funds' (c075, c079, c109) without saying they are the same.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'only so much time to the business of the Company as is reasonably required' is a vague commitment whose boundary a court could be asked to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c110 states the same undertaking as 'such of its business time ... as may be necessary to perform its obligations' — similar but not identical formulations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual disclosure about counsel; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c118.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'setting a purchase price ... which is not less than any of the following: (i) ... (ii) ... or (iii)' is ambiguous on its face — 'not less than any of' can mean at least the greatest, or at least one of them, and the 'or' pushes toward the weaker reading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its closing sentence deems affiliate seller financing not to be a 'Related Party Loan', qualifying c051's definition and the c052 20% cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Company expects to purchase mortgage loans from, or later into co-investment agreements with, R.E. Loans' is missing a verb, and 'Sponsored Investment Funds or Private Clients' are capitalised but never defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c075 covers the same subject with a different and fuller set of criteria, and the criteria here are simply delegated to the Note Purchase Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'primarily in the United States', 'occasional loans' and 'a strict set of guidelines' are soft, but the section is framed as policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c063 permits up to 20% in non-U.S. properties, which is the concrete content of 'primarily'; the two read together coherently enough.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare two-line table — 'Land 50%' — with no statement of what value the ratio is taken against or how 'Improved Property' and 'Land' are bounded; a short phrase carrying real construction risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c064 says the ratios 'generally will not exceed' these percentages and allows as-completed appraisals and a purchase-money exception, materially loosening what the table states as fixed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Most Company loans are expected to be secured by a first deed of trust' is an expectation, not a covenant, while the 20% junior-lien cap is stated as a limit; the pairing is uneven.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cap is measured against 'the Company's entire Loan Portfolio', a term not defined anywhere else in the instrument (compare 'total Company assets' in c052 and 'total Company Capital' in c063).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'limit its lending activity primarily to' plus a 20% carve-out is internally odd, and the cap is measured against 'total Company Capital', an undefined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c060 and c083 describe the lending universe as real estate 'located primarily in the United States, its territories and possessions', which does not obviously accommodate a fixed 20% foreign allowance measured on a different base.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'generally will not exceed the percentages stated above, based a valuation ... as determined by either the Manager or an independent written appraisal' contains a dropped word and lets the Manager set value unilaterally; 'generally' undoes the limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the fixed ratios in c061 and, by deeming affiliate purchase-money financing not to be a Related Party Loan, carves an exception out of c051/c052.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will vary at the discretion of the Manager' and 'generally have a term of between one (1) and six (6) years' are loose but transparently so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A six-year loan term made late in the offering could outrun the December 31, 2014 Note Maturity Date in c089 and the Company term in c106 — a real but soft mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'such considerations are subordinate to' a collateral test is definite, though it produces a striking result.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Lending to borrowers 'in default under other of their obligations' or without qualifying income is difficult to square with c020's promise of 'conservatively underwritten' loans and no sub-prime activity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short chapeau introducing escrow conditions; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its list is c068–c071; see the note on c070, which is not a condition at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Satisfactory title insurance coverage' leaves the standard of satisfaction unstated, but the amount is fixed to the loan principal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c071's requirement that documents name the Company; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Satisfactory fire and casualty insurance ... or only casualty insurance in the event of a Loan secured by unimproved land' is workable, though 'satisfactory' is unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 'VII. Risk Factors – Uninsured Losses', a heading that does not appear in the Risk Factors section (the nearest is c151, 'Inadequate Preservation of Collateral').

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item (c) is not a condition to disbursement at all but a statement that no mortgage insurance will be obtained, so its place in an enumerated list of escrow conditions is a genuine list-scope defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits inside the c067 chapeau ('will be instructed not to disburse any funds until the following conditions are met'), which it cannot satisfy as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will name the Company as payee and beneficiary or additional loss insured, as applicable' is definite enough in context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c068/c069 and with c072's servicing arrangements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'It is anticipated that all Company loans will be serviced' by the Servicer states expectation, not obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Payments may be mailed to the Servicer's trust account, which sits against c071's insistence that Company investments not be held in any nominee's name — a mild tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'must be purchased from the Company by the Manager or its affiliate rf the Loan is in default more than 90 days' contains a corrupted word, and the compressed semicolon structure obscures which limits attach to what.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the c052 20% cap as tested only 'upon the closing of the Related Party Loan in question', directly at odds with c052's 'at any time ... at such time'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Manager may purchase loans from unaffiliated parties for a premium' names the wrong actor — the paragraph is about the Company's purchases — and 'fair and reasonable' is unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The bar on purchasing loans in default sits against c058 and c079, which contemplate affiliate dealings in defaulted loans, and against c075's 'fully performing loan' criterion stated differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or to achieve comparable with Sponsored Investment Funds' is missing a noun, and 'a purchase from, sale to, of a co-investment with' contains a further error; the criteria themselves ('fair market value or better', 'customary for the geographical market') are soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates c059 with a materially fuller set of criteria and uses 'Sponsored Investment Funds' where c055 defined 'Other Sponsored Investment Funds'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'None of the Company ... is precluded from (i) selling ... or (ii) from making a loan' is grammatically broken, and the proviso's reach across both limbs is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes affiliated Noteholder transactions to 'the criteria established by the Note Purchase Agreement', the same delegation used in c059 and c075; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'After the second year of the Company's term' and '20% of the capital of the Company' are both unanchored — the term's start is not fixed here and 'capital' is not a defined measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c106 defines the Company's term only by its termination events, so 'the second year of the Company's term' has no fixed start date anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entirely permissive ('may be retained', 'if the Manager believes'); little for a court to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Funding a reserve 'from any source, including capital raised from the sale of Notes' fits c019's use-of-proceeds language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not expect to engage in real estate operations in the ordinary course' followed by broad permission to sell to affiliates is a hedged formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against c020's flat statement that the Company 'will not source loans for the purpose of resale' and against c074's rule that purchased loans not be in default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Explanatory description of leverage; the terms are used in their ordinary sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 'Risks and Other Important Factors – Risks of Leverage', a heading that does not exist in Section VII, and overlaps with c108's Company Borrowing regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'accepted in the discretion of the Managing Member' uses a term the instrument never defines (elsewhere 'Manager' or 'Managing Directors'), and 'Noteholders' is redefined here differently from c015.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c088 says subscriptions are accepted 'by the Manager, in its sole discretion' — a different actor from the 'Managing Member' named here, and c185 repeats the same stray term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare identification of the issuing entity; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'such other directly related activities ... as the Manager deems reasonably necessary or appropriate' is a general catch-all appended to enumerated purposes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c113 protects the 'general purpose of the Company' from amendment without Noteholder approval, so the elasticity of this purpose clause matters; c079 also disclaims ordinary-course real estate operations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company may admit additional or substitute managers' is a bare permission with no procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against c109, which bars the Manager from withdrawing as 'the sole manager' without a Majority in Interest, and against c097's description of a single initial member/manager.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'owned by Barney Ng and Kelly Ng, a Managing Director of the Manager' has a dangling appositive, and 'Servicer' is defined collectively for 'one or more qualified servicing entities'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c014 says the Manager only 'expects to hire' Bar-K, while this says the initial Servicer 'shall be' Bar-K; a difference in firmness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional paragraph; the OCR garbling of 'Program' does not change meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'There is no minimum or maximum amount of Investor Capital' matches c015; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A minimum investment is 20,000 Units, in the discretion of the Manager' is genuinely unclear — whether the minimum binds, or whether the Manager may waive or raise it, cannot be told from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision states a minimum subscription, so nothing resolves the ambiguity; c183's acceptance discretion is the nearest analogue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'accredited investors within the meaning of the United States Securities Act of 1933' is a definite external standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c173 states the standard as Rule 501 under the Securities Act, and c175–c179 give a list that is narrower in places than Rule 501 (e.g. only irrevocable trusts).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Maturity Date' is defined twice and differently — first as the December 31, 2014 date subject to a six-month extension, then as 'the last day of the Note's term' — and a rate set 'in the sole discretion of the Manager' subject to a floor 'for a calendar year' leaves the floor's measuring period unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c016 describes the same rate as 'a minimum average rate of eight percent (8%) annualized' and c012 as 'approximately 8.00% or more', while c124 treats the Notes as contingent debt paying 'additional interest' — several inconsistent accounts of one payment term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Payment mechanics stated concretely; 'Principal' is defined at the point of issuance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c093's Closing Account mechanics and c087's Unit pricing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'provided that the Noteholder is a qualified investor at the time of the closing' uses 'qualified investor', a term not defined (compare 'accredited investor' in c088/c173).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'no additional subscriptions ... will be accepted by the Manager for any closing after the final closing' sits against c092, which lets the Manager solicit additional Units 'from time to time' without that limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The passage mixes a Noteholder request with a Company offer ('In order to accept an offer to sell additional Units by the Company'), and again uses the undefined 'qualified investor'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c091's bar on subscriptions after the final closing, it is unclear whether the Manager's later requests are subject to that cut-off.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Account mechanics are stated definitely, including who keeps interest earned.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c090 and c183 (rejection of subscriptions and return of deposits).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Minimum Holding Period' is defined as a date rather than a period, and 'unless either of such conditions is waived by the Company' leaves an entirely discretionary prepayment regime.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c017's summary says a Noteholder 'may not request prepayment ... until it has held the Note for a minimum of one year', which is a bar on requesting rather than on the prepayment date fixed here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Collateral Agent must act 'on terms required by the Manager' yet 'only to the extent that such terms or actions are not prohibited under the Noteholder Agreements' — a proviso whose reach cannot be assessed from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c109 forbids any Lien on the Collateral without a Majority in Interest, yet this clause and c108 let the Collateral Agent subordinate the Noteholders' interest to a Company Borrowing without such a vote.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acceleration on bankruptcy is subject to an exception where obligations 'have been assumed by an affiliate of or successor in interest to the Company', a materially open-ended escape from the acceleration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That exception sits oddly with c109's requirement of Noteholder approval for any merger, consolidation or dissolution, and with c018's characterisation of Noteholders as secured creditors.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'with the requisite approval of members' is undefined, and the Manager's admission power is otherwise discretionary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c084 permits admission of 'additional or substitute managers' on different terms; the two membership/management provisions are not aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed $25,000 minimum contribution and a permission to buy Notes; both definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c015's statement that affiliates may buy Notes on the same terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'on or prior to the last day of the end of the sixth full quarter after the Initial Closing (estimated June 30, 2009)' is clumsy and the parenthetical estimate does not track the formula from a December 1, 2007 start.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c015 says the initial closing is expected 'on or before December 3, 2007' with closings 'through May 1, 2009' — different dates for the same events.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The management fee is stated with a formula, a frequency and a measuring date; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c038's table entry; consistent.
